rationale: VERSION 2.1.0 -> 3.0.0: rebuilt the distribution around the demonstrated maze grammar instead of treating a border-only room as an easy example.; Added a 25% default-only prior over all five complete linked public input profiles, with D4 transforms and endpoint-color relabeling. The prior preserves each profile's dimensions, full wall topology, endpoint grouping, and pair geometry as one joint object.; General draws now use a complete color-8 border plus one to five interior dividers with gaps, one to three exactly paired endpoint colors, Manhattan separation at least three, and canonical paths that exist on the original grid and do not overlap.; Calibrated bands to 7..10 by 8..12 with one or two pairs for easy, 9..13 by 10..15 with two pairs for medium, and 12..16 by 14..18 with two or three pairs for hard. All eight non-wall ARC colors are sampled.; Replaced the old post-hoc connectivity check with constructive path reservation and a bounded 128-attempt loop plus an exact axis-honest fallback. The fallback was never used in either 15000-draw census.; Reduced the public interface to three exact observable controls: grid_h, grid_w, and n_pairs. Removed the old band-dependent rejection behavior; every declared global boundary is exact or rejected before construction.; Added strict call validation, observational self_check, observe_overrides, an independent Python rule mirror, exact linked-profile extraction, deterministic fresh returns, and a RULE_HASH pin.; Added ten focused regression groups covering all five public pairs, both disjoint profile samples, all 21 override cases, smallest 7x8 three-pair feasibility, deterministic/fresh/global-RNG behavior, structural mutations, source pinning, and broader rule semantics.
summary: Treat color 8 as walls. For each other color that occurs exactly twice, in ascending color order, find the canonical breadth-first shortest path on the original input through zero cells or that pair's goal, using neighbor order up, down, left, right. Paint every cell of each found path with its endpoint color. Ignore non-pair colors, leave unreachable pairs unchanged, and let a later color overwrite an earlier one where paths overlap.
